questions.question: Why does measure_latency run warmup iterations before recording times?
options: To avoid including one-time setup or compilation costs in the steady-state measurements
To make the model train on five extra batches
To increase the input resolution before timing
To replace p50 with the first observed duration
questions.explanation: Warmup calls establish the execution path; only the following timed iterations are sorted into p50, p95, p99, and mean.

questions.question: What does parameter_count(model) include?
options: Only convolution kernel heights
The number of scalar values in every model parameter tensor
The number of input pixels seen during one run
The median latency in milliseconds
questions.explanation: It sums p.numel() for p in model.parameters(), including trainable and non-trainable parameter tensors.

questions.question: In flops_estimate, why is a convolution's count multiplied by c_in_per_group rather than all input channels?
options: The model never reads input channels during convolution
A group means one output pixel is reused only once
Grouped and depthwise convolutions connect each output channel to only its group's inputs
The factor counts parameters instead of multiply-adds
questions.explanation: The hook uses 2*c_in_per_group*c_out*kh*kw*h*w, accounting for a multiply and add for each connected input.

questions.question: Which timing statistic answers 'how long did at least 95% of measured calls take' most directly?
options: p50_ms
mean_ms
parameter_count
p95_ms
questions.explanation: The p95 percentile describes the upper tail below which roughly 95% of recorded latencies fall.

questions.question: Why does measure_latency call torch.cuda.synchronize() around CUDA timings?
options: CUDA work is asynchronous, so synchronization makes the measured interval include kernel completion
It converts CUDA tensors to CPU labels
It reduces the model's parameter count
It turns p95 latency into throughput
questions.explanation: Without synchronization, the CPU timer could stop before queued GPU work finishes and report an unrealistically small duration.

questions.question: When choosing an edge backbone from compare_backbones, what must be considered together?
options: Only the model name alphabetically
Accuracy needs, parameter/FLOP budget, and measured tail latency
Only the number of output classes
The training set's file extension
questions.explanation: An edge deployment has a latency and memory budget as well as a quality target; the script reports parameters, GFLOPs, and p50/p95 latency to expose the tradeoff.
